correctness.rationale: Every good must be alone for m=4, since an empty agent would violate inter-EF1 if any agent held two goods. At m=5 exactly one agent holds two goods, one a minimum-valued item; singleton agents must value their own good at least the smaller of that pair. The two center-EFX inequalities reduce to u+v>=s+t and s+t+e>=max(u,v). The proof supplies explicit allocations in a+d<=b+c and a+d>b+c cases. Appending a good no larger than old maximum preserves four-good feasibility. Rank-of-appended observation R is uniform independent of sorted spacings; exponential order gaps are independent with rates 5,4,3,2,1 and uniform gaps normalized iid exponentials. Integration produces p10=4/105 for exponential and 1/120 for uniform, from which exact remaining table entries follow. Direct independent enumerator checked all 461 positive integer multiset profiles within its stated finite range, examining 23741 allocation cases until fairness witness; finite verification is corroboration, not an unrestricted proof.
